meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Usually как будто.

examples.text: Он смотрит, как будто знает всё.
examples.trans: He looks as if he knows everything.

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And what about the wine and fruit?

examples.text: Смотри, это электрогитара для Лёши. А тебе я взял чилийское вино и ягоды.
examples.trans: Look, this is an electric guitar for Lyosha. And for you I brought Chilean wine and berries.

meanings.note: usually short form: я виноват / я виновата

examples.text: Она ни в чём не виновата.
examples.trans: She is not to blame for anything.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не гони меня. Я знаю, что я виноват.
examples.trans: Please, don't chase me away. I know it's my fault.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.
I am not going to steal a dog.

examples.text: Аркашенька, ну это же бред! Я не буду воровать собаку.
examples.trans: Arkashenka, come on, this is nonsense! I'm not going to steal a dog.

meanings.note: Проводить время = to spend time.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: + genitive.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: irregular feminine declension with stem дочер-

examples.text: Простите, это собака дочери. Я с ней гуляю пока.
examples.trans: Sorry, it's my daughter's dog. I'm walking her for now.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Ещё больше = even more.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Secondary conversational sense ('booking') (commission or reservation) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.

meanings.note: To bring an activity to an end.

examples.text: Марина, давай заканчивать эту опасную акцию.
examples.trans: Marina, let's end this dangerous protest.
The craftsmen are already finishing the complex repair.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Никто, кроме... = nobody except.

examples.text: Ни у кого в городе нет денег, кроме Игнатьева.
examples.trans: Nobody in town has any money, except Ignatyev.
I am speaking seriously, no joking!

meanings.note: На лечение = for treatment.

examples.text: И бабушку на лечение в Израиль отправил.
examples.trans: And he sent our grandmother to Israel for treatment.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?
But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: to send (a person, a letter, a message)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'править').

examples.text: И бабушку на лечение в Израиль отправил.
examples.trans: And he sent our grandmother to Israel for treatment.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу. Что, плохая работа?
examples.trans: You were offered a job. What, is it a bad job?

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: + instrumental (where).
+ accusative (where to).
Под мою ответственность.

examples.trans: The cat is under the table.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

поддаваться.gloss: to give in, to yield (to); to let someone win

meanings.note: + dative: поддаваться лечению/гипнозу = respond to treatment/hypnosis

meanings.en: to let someone win (in a game)
meanings.note: + dative

examples.text: Ничего, Макс с детства не поддаётся гипнозу.
examples.trans: Don't worry, Max hasn't been susceptible to hypnosis since childhood.

examples.text: Шеф, да я же вам поддавался!
examples.trans: Chef, I was letting you win!

examples.text: Или ты лечению не поддаёшься, или он плохой специалист.
examples.trans: Either you don't respond to treatment, or he's a bad specialist.

meanings.note: вызывать подозрения = to raise suspicion

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, упаковка маскирующая. Не вызывает подозрений.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, the packaging is camouflage. It doesn't raise suspicion.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
+ dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь').

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Провести время. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'вести').
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'вести').

examples.trans: We spent the evening at home.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.
Didn't they let him out of the nuthouse?

examples.text: За мои деньги хочешь меня в психушку отправить?
examples.trans: You want to send me to the nuthouse with my own money?

meanings.note: Inquiry into facts.

examples.text: Тогда я проведу собственное расследование и найду вора.
examples.trans: Then I'll carry out my own investigation and find the thief.

meanings.en: dear, darling, my friend (in address: родной мой)
meanings.note: Often used ironically.
родной брат = full brother; родной город = hometown

examples.text: Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: Well then, my dear friend, to you!

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска! Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk! Well then, my dear friend, to you!

meanings.note: Animal or food.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: У нас севрюга в меню появилась?
examples.trans: Did stellate sturgeon appear on our menu?
I have never eaten stellate sturgeon.

examples.text: Новый заказ: севрюга в белом вине.
examples.trans: New order: stellate sturgeon in white wine.

examples.text: Я хочу купить собственную строительную компанию.
examples.trans: I want to buy my own construction company.

meanings.note: Used for men and women.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
